template_params.base: accounts with MRR at the end of the month before

prompt: Wannes, the head of customer success, is preparing the quarterly business review and asks for LedgerLoop's logo churn rate in each month from February to September 2025. Use mrr_monthly: one row per account and month, with the account's MRR in euros on the month's last day; an account with no row in a month had no MRR then. A month's accounts at start are the accounts with MRR on the last day of the month before. Its churned accounts are those of them with no MRR on the month's own last day; an account that leaves and comes back within one month has MRR on both last days, so it has not churned. An account that is new or comes back during a month is not among that month's accounts at start. Return one row for each month from February to September 2025, with four columns in this order: month, the first day of the month; accounts_at_start; churned_accounts; and logo_churn_pct, 100 times churned_accounts divided by accounts_at_start (2.5 for 2.5%), rounded to 1 decimal. Sort by month from oldest to newest.
hints: Next, take each account with MRR at the end of a month from January to August 2025, and give it the month after as the month being measured.
Keep every one of those accounts when you look for its MRR in the month after, and count the ones with nothing there as churned.
why_this_works: Starting from the accounts with MRR at the end of the month before keeps the leavers in the base, and an account with no row in the next month is exactly one that churned.
